comment: Attributes one side's emitted document states and the other's omits, where BC's own reader produces the SAME object either way (#4357). These are NOT declared differences: on every entry here the two derivations agree, and what is declared is that the agreement carries no information. tests/expectations/metadata-equivalence/allowlist.json is the other file and means the opposite — a tolerated DISAGREEMENT. Measured on BC 28.1.49838.53910 over the Business Foundation and System Application bundles, 1,286 objects; docs/metadata-equivalence.md#unobservable-omissions has the table and the method. An undeclared omission fails the run, and an entry matching nothing fails it too unless it is versionContingent — which here means 'fewer than 10 of the 1,286 objects carry it on the measured build', a population one BC version's object churn can remove.

omissions.reason: BC's emitted document states this attribute and the runner's does not, on 558 occurrence(s) across the two 28.1.49838.53910 ground-truth bundles, with value(s) 'Manual', 'StaticAutomatic'. BC's own reader produces the same object with the attribute and without it, so the member-for-member comparison agrees and that agreement says nothing about whether the runner's derivation is right. UNTRIAGED: #4400 decides whether the runner should state it or whether saying less is legitimate here.
